full_judgment: 144. But we fail to agree with the above argument for three reasons". Firstly, to our knowledge, there is no law which requires the investigating officer to take a person in remand on the same date of the remand order or within a specified period thereafter. Secondly, the remand order dated 6-9-1998 became effective on 26-9-1998 for three days, and Shahid was produced on 27-9-1998 at an odd hour i.e. 4-30 PM. There is nothing on record to show that Shahid, on his production before the Magistrate on 27-9-1998 it 4-30, refused to make any statement or otherwise reported any torture or influence. So, there was no illegality in. sending him back to the custody of investigating officer who produced Shahid on the next day (28-5-1998) i.e. before the expiry of the remand period, and thus the second confessional statement was recorded within the legally approved period of remand. Thirdly, there is no law, to our knowledge, about the recording of a confessional statement within a specified period during investigation. Moreover, his evidence being inculpatory as well as exculpatory, we have considered it in the context of totality of the evidence.
